blocks.text: Drug development is the process of testing the discovered drug and preparing it for public use.

items: Preclinical research: compounds are tested in vitro (cell cultures) and in vivo (animals) for safety, toxicity and efficacy before human trials.

Clinical trials, in people: phase 1 tests a small group (20-100) of healthy volunteers for safety and dosage; phase 2 a larger group (100-300) of patients for effectiveness and side effects; phase 3 large-scale trials (1,000-3,000) confirm efficacy and monitor adverse reactions.
Regulatory review: agencies such as the FDA or EMA examine all the data from the trials and approve or reject the drug before it reaches the market.
Manufacturing and marketing: the approved drug is produced on a large scale and made available.
Post-marketing surveillance: the drug is monitored after release for long-term and rare side effects.

blocks.title: In Pakistan
blocks.text: The book names the FDA (United States) and the EMA (Europe). In Pakistan medicines are registered and regulated by the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (DRAP).

blocks.prompt: Which clinical trial phase tests 100-300 patients for effectiveness and side effects?

items: Preclinical (cells, animals), then phases 1, 2, 3 in people.
